title: Hypotheses & Regrets
subtitle: Imagine alternatives with si-clauses and talk about what you would have done differently

lessons.title: Si j'avais su
lessons.description: Build hypothetical sentences with si + imparfait and the conditionnel présent to imagine unreal or unlikely situations.

blocks.heading: Hypothetical si-clauses
blocks.body: To imagine a present or future situation that isn't real — or that you think is unlikely — French pairs "si + imparfait" with the conditionnel présent. This is very different from a real condition ("si + présent, futur"): here you're stepping into an imaginary version of reality.

examples.french: Si j'avais plus de temps, je voyagerais plus souvent.
examples.english: If I had more time, I would travel more often.

examples.french: Si tu savais la vérité, tu serais surpris.
examples.english: If you knew the truth, you would be surprised.

examples.french: Nous partirions en vacances si nous avions de l'argent.
examples.english: We would go on vacation if we had money.

examples.french: Si elle parlait mieux anglais, elle trouverait un travail à l'étranger.
examples.english: If she spoke English better, she'd find a job abroad.

examples.french: Si j'étais toi, je changerais de métier.
examples.english: If I were you, I would change jobs.

blocks.tip: The si-clause NEVER takes the conditionnel — only imparfait. The conditionnel always lives in the result clause.

blocks.heading: Building the conditionnel présent
blocks.body: The conditionnel présent uses the same stem as the futur simple (usually the infinitive) plus the imparfait endings: -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient. If you already know a verb's futur stem, you already know its conditionnel.

examples.french: Je parlerais, tu finirais, il vendrait...
examples.english: I would speak, you would finish, he would sell...

examples.french: Je serais content si tu venais.
examples.english: I would be happy if you came.

examples.french: Elle aurait le temps si elle s'organisait mieux.
examples.english: She would have the time if she organized herself better.

examples.french: Il ferait un effort si on le lui demandait.
examples.english: He would make an effort if we asked him to.

examples.french: Nous irions à la plage s'il faisait beau.
examples.english: We would go to the beach if the weather were nice.

blocks.tip: Irregular stems are shared with the futur: pouvoir → pourr-, vouloir → voudr-, devoir → devr-, savoir → saur-, venir → viendr-.

blocks.heading: Giving advice and floating ideas
blocks.body: "Si j'étais toi" or "à ta place" introduce gentle advice. "Et si + imparfait ?" — with no result clause at all — is a common, soft way to suggest an idea, roughly "What if...?"

examples.french: Et si on partait plus tôt ?
examples.english: What if we left earlier?

examples.french: Si j'étais à ta place, j'accepterais l'offre.
examples.english: If I were in your place, I would accept the offer.

examples.french: Et si tu lui parlais franchement ?
examples.english: What if you talked to him honestly?

examples.french: À ta place, je réfléchirais avant de répondre.
examples.english: In your place, I would think it over before answering.

blocks.tip: "Et si...?" alone, without a second clause, is one of the most natural ways French speakers make suggestions.

blocks.heading: Conditionnel présent: full formation
blocks.body: Regular verbs take the infinitive as the stem (dropping the final -e for -re verbs) and add: -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient. Learn the small set of irregular stems and you can build the conditionnel for almost any verb.

examples.french: parler → je parlerais, nous parlerions
examples.english: to speak → I would speak, we would speak

examples.french: finir → tu finirais, ils finiraient
examples.english: to finish → you would finish, they would finish

examples.french: vendre → elle vendrait, vous vendriez
examples.english: to sell → she would sell, you would sell

examples.french: être → je serais / avoir → j'aurais
examples.english: to be → I would be / to have → I would have

examples.french: pouvoir → je pourrais / vouloir → je voudrais / devoir → je devrais
examples.english: to be able → I could / to want → I would want / must → I should

examples.french: savoir → je saurais / venir → je viendrais / voir → je verrais
examples.english: to know → I would know / to come → I would come / to see → I would see

blocks.tip: The conditionnel endings are identical to the imparfait endings — only the stem changes.

blocks.heading: Putting the pattern to work
blocks.body: "Si + imparfait" sets up an imaginary condition; the conditionnel présent gives its imagined result. The two clauses can swap order, and "si" becomes "s'" only before "il/ils" (never before "elle" or "on" in careful writing, though "s'on" is avoided altogether — French uses "si l'on" instead).

examples.french: Si j'avais un jardin, je cultiverais des légumes.
examples.english: If I had a garden, I would grow vegetables.

examples.french: S'il faisait plus chaud, on mangerait dehors.
examples.english: If it were warmer, we would eat outside.

examples.french: Que ferais-tu si tu gagnais un million d'euros ?
examples.english: What would you do if you won a million euros?

examples.french: Si l'on te posait la question, que répondrais-tu ?
examples.english: If someone asked you the question, how would you answer?

blocks.tip: Common mistake: never write "si j'aurais" — the si-clause always stays in the imparfait, never the conditionnel.

passages.title: Une autre vie
passages.french:
Parfois, je me demande à quoi ressemblerait ma vie si j'avais fait d'autres choix.
Si j'avais étudié la médecine au lieu du droit, je travaillerais peut-être dans un hôpital aujourd'hui.
Aujourd'hui, je passe mes journées avec des dossiers et des contrats, loin des blouses blanches.
Si seulement j'avais écouté mon professeur de sciences, qui voyait en moi une future chercheuse !
Mais si je n'avais pas choisi le droit, je ne travaillerais sans doute pas avec Camille, ma collègue et meilleure amie.
Et si je vivais à l'étranger, comme j'en rêvais à vingt ans ?
Je parlerais sans doute une autre langue couramment, et je verrais mes parents beaucoup moins souvent.
Franchement, je ne regrette pas grand-chose : chaque choix mène à une vie différente, ni meilleure ni pire.
Si je prévoyais tout à l'avance, la vie serait sans doute moins surprenante.
Et si, finalement, le plus important n'était pas de deviner l'avenir, mais d'accepter ses choix ?
À ta place, je ne perdrais pas trop de temps à imaginer un autre scénario.
Personne ne connaît la vie qu'on n'a pas vécue — et c'est peut-être très bien ainsi.
passages.english:
Sometimes I wonder what my life would look like if I had made other choices.
If I had studied medicine instead of law, I would maybe be working in a hospital today.
Today, I spend my days with files and contracts, far from white coats.
If only I had listened to my science teacher, who saw a future researcher in me!
But if I hadn't chosen law, I probably wouldn't be working with Camille, my colleague and best friend.
And what if I lived abroad, like I used to dream of at twenty?
I would probably speak another language fluently, and I would see my parents much less often.
Honestly, I don't regret much: every choice leads to a different life, neither better nor worse.
If I planned everything in advance, life would probably be less surprising.
And what if, in the end, the most important thing wasn't guessing the future, but accepting one's choices?
In your place, I wouldn't waste too much time imagining another scenario.
Nobody knows the life they didn't live — and maybe that's just fine.

lessons.title: Les regrets
lessons.description: Express regret about the past with "j'aurais dû" and get introduced to the conditionnel passé.

blocks.heading: "J'aurais dû": the classic regret
blocks.body: The single most useful phrase for regret in French is "j'aurais dû" + infinitive — "I should have...". It's the conditionnel passé of "devoir", and it's how French speakers admit, gently or painfully, that they made the wrong call.

examples.french: J'aurais dû t'écouter.
examples.english: I should have listened to you.

examples.french: Tu aurais dû me le dire plus tôt.
examples.english: You should have told me sooner.

examples.french: On aurait dû réserver à l'avance.
examples.english: We should have booked in advance.

examples.french: Elle n'aurait pas dû accepter ce poste.
examples.english: She shouldn't have accepted that job.

examples.french: Vous auriez dû vérifier avant de partir.
examples.english: You should have checked before leaving.

blocks.tip: "J'aurais dû" always pairs with an infinitive: j'aurais dû partir, dire, réfléchir...

blocks.heading: Introducing the conditionnel passé
blocks.body: The conditionnel passé describes what would have happened, under different circumstances, in the past. It's built like the passé composé, but with the auxiliary (avoir or être) in the conditionnel présent instead of the présent: aurais/serais + past participle.

examples.french: J'aurais aimé voyager davantage.
examples.english: I would have liked to travel more.

examples.french: Elle serait venue si elle avait pu.
examples.english: She would have come if she had been able to.

examples.french: Nous aurions réussi avec un peu plus de temps.
examples.english: We would have succeeded with a little more time.

examples.french: Ils ne se seraient jamais rencontrés autrement.
examples.english: They would never have met otherwise.

blocks.tip: Reflexive and être-verbs still use être in the conditionnel passé: je serais parti(e), elle se serait trompée.

blocks.heading: Living with regret, gracefully
blocks.body: Beyond "j'aurais dû", French has a whole vocabulary for processing regret without dwelling on it forever: "tant pis", "c'est comme ça", "on ne peut rien y changer", and the very useful "avec le recul" (looking back, in hindsight).

examples.french: Avec le recul, j'aurais dû faire des études plus courtes.
examples.english: Looking back, I should have studied for less time.

examples.french: Tant pis, ce n'est pas grave.
examples.english: Oh well, it's not a big deal.

examples.french: On ne peut rien y changer maintenant.
examples.english: There's nothing we can do about it now.

examples.french: C'est comme ça ; il faut avancer.
examples.english: That's just how it is; you have to move forward.

blocks.tip: French speakers often soften a regret with "tant pis" — it signals acceptance rather than defeat.

blocks.heading: Formation: auxiliary + past participle
blocks.body: The conditionnel passé = conditionnel présent of avoir or être + past participle. Choose the same auxiliary you would use in the passé composé, and apply the same agreement rules for être-verbs and preceding direct objects.

examples.french: j'aurais parlé, tu aurais fini, il aurait vendu
examples.english: I would have spoken, you would have finished, he would have sold

examples.french: je serais allé(e), elle serait partie, nous serions venu(e)s
examples.english: I would have gone, she would have left, we would have come

examples.french: je me serais trompé(e), ils se seraient perdus
examples.english: I would have been wrong, they would have gotten lost

examples.french: Elle aurait pu réussir avec plus de soutien.
examples.english: She could have succeeded with more support.

blocks.tip: "J'aurais dû", "j'aurais pu", "j'aurais voulu" are the three regret verbs to master first: should have, could have, would have wanted to.

blocks.heading: Negative and question forms
blocks.body: In the negative, "ne...pas" wraps around the auxiliary, not the past participle: "je n'aurais pas dû". In questions, invert the subject and auxiliary as usual: "Aurais-tu accepté ?"

examples.french: Je n'aurais pas dû lui répondre comme ça.
examples.english: I shouldn't have answered him like that.

examples.french: Elle n'aurait jamais accepté ce compromis.
examples.english: She would never have accepted that compromise.

examples.french: Aurais-tu fait la même chose ?
examples.english: Would you have done the same thing?

examples.french: Qu'aurait-il dit à ma place ?
examples.english: What would he have said in my place?

blocks.tip: Don't confuse this with "j'ai dû" (I had to) — "j'aurais dû" always means "I should have" (but didn't).

passages.title: Le message que je n'ai jamais envoyé
passages.french:
Cher journal, aujourd'hui j'ai repensé à toute cette année.
J'aurais dû accepter ce poste à Lyon, mais j'ai eu peur du changement.
Avec le recul, cette peur n'avait aucun sens.
J'aurais gagné en confiance, et j'aurais rencontré des gens formidables.
Au lieu de ça, je suis resté dans mon petit bureau, à me demander ce que ma vie aurait pu être.
Je m'en veux aussi d'avoir perdu contact avec Sophie, ma meilleure amie d'université.
Nous nous serions sans doute revues plus souvent si j'avais fait le premier pas.
Hélas, la fierté m'en a empêché.
Heureusement, il n'est jamais trop tard pour tirer une leçon de ses erreurs.
Demain, j'écrirai enfin ce message que j'aurais dû envoyer il y a des mois.
Après tout, mieux vaut regretter d'avoir essayé que de ne jamais avoir essayé du tout.
Alors, malgré tout, je tourne la page et j'avance.
passages.english:
Dear diary, today I thought back over this whole year.
I should have accepted that job in Lyon, but I was scared of change.
Looking back, that fear made no sense.
I would have gained confidence, and I would have met wonderful people.
Instead, I stayed in my little office, wondering what my life could have been.
I'm also upset with myself for having lost touch with Sophie, my best friend from university.
We probably would have seen each other more often if I had made the first move.
Alas, pride stopped me.
Fortunately, it's never too late to learn a lesson from one's mistakes.
Tomorrow, I will finally write that message I should have sent months ago.
After all, it's better to regret having tried than to never have tried at all.
So, despite everything, I'm turning the page and moving forward.

lessons.title: Imaginer autrement
lessons.description: Combine si + plus-que-parfait with the conditionnel passé to tell counterfactual stories about the past.

blocks.heading: The third condition: si + plus-que-parfait
blocks.body: To imagine how the past could have gone differently, French uses "si + plus-que-parfait" for the condition and the conditionnel passé for the imagined result. This is the classic "if I had known, I would have..." — a fully counterfactual, closed-past scenario.

examples.french: Si j'avais su, je ne serais jamais parti.
examples.english: If I had known, I would never have left.

examples.french: Si tu m'avais appelé, je serais venu tout de suite.
examples.english: If you had called me, I would have come right away.

examples.french: Nous aurions réussi si nous avions mieux préparé le projet.
examples.english: We would have succeeded if we had prepared the project better.

examples.french: Elle n'aurait pas déménagé si elle avait trouvé du travail ici.
examples.english: She wouldn't have moved if she had found work here.

blocks.tip: Think in three layers: si + imparfait → conditionnel présent (unit's lesson 1) versus si + plus-que-parfait → conditionnel passé (this lesson) — the further back the condition, the further back the tense.

blocks.heading: Mixed timelines: past cause, present effect
blocks.body: Sometimes a past condition still echoes into today. In that case, French can mix a plus-que-parfait si-clause with a conditionnel présent result, to show a past decision shaping a present reality.

examples.french: Si j'avais accepté ce poste, je vivrais à Montréal aujourd'hui.
examples.english: If I had accepted that job, I would be living in Montreal today.

examples.french: Si nous ne nous étions pas rencontrés, ma vie serait complètement différente.
examples.english: If we hadn't met, my life would be completely different.

examples.french: Si elle n'avait pas insisté, je ne saurais pas cuisiner aujourd'hui.
examples.english: If she hadn't insisted, I wouldn't know how to cook today.

blocks.tip: This mixed pattern is advanced but very natural — it links a closed past event to an ongoing present consequence.

blocks.heading: Telling a counterfactual story
blocks.body: To narrate a whole "what if" scenario, combine the grammar with storytelling connectors: "et si...", "dans cette autre vie...", "qui sait...", "au lieu de...". These frame the imagined version of events as a story, not just a grammar drill.

examples.french: Et si, ce jour-là, j'avais pris l'autre train ?
examples.english: What if, that day, I had taken the other train?

examples.french: Dans cette autre vie, je serais peut-être devenu musicien.
examples.english: In that other life, I might have become a musician.

examples.french: Qui sait ce qui se serait passé ?
examples.english: Who knows what would have happened?

examples.french: Au lieu de rester, j'aurais pu tout quitter.
examples.english: Instead of staying, I could have left everything.

blocks.tip: "Qui sait...?" is a great way to end a counterfactual story — it leaves the alternate life gracefully unresolved.

blocks.heading: Three conditions, side by side
blocks.body: By now you can build all three French conditions. Real: "si + présent, futur" (Si j'ai le temps, je viendrai). Hypothetical present: "si + imparfait, conditionnel présent" (Si j'avais le temps, je viendrais). Counterfactual past: "si + plus-que-parfait, conditionnel passé" (Si j'avais eu le temps, je serais venu).

examples.french: Si j'ai le temps, je viendrai. (réel)
examples.english: If I have time, I will come. (real)

examples.french: Si j'avais le temps, je viendrais. (hypothétique)
examples.english: If I had time, I would come. (hypothetical)

examples.french: Si j'avais eu le temps, je serais venu. (contrefactuel)
examples.english: If I had had time, I would have come. (counterfactual)

examples.french: Si nous avions su, nous aurions réagi autrement.
examples.english: If we had known, we would have reacted differently.

blocks.tip: The plus-que-parfait itself follows the passé composé pattern, just with avoir/être in the imparfait: j'avais eu, j'étais parti(e).

blocks.heading: Narrating a full "what if" story
blocks.body: A good counterfactual story usually moves through three moves: set the real fact (passé composé/imparfait), pivot with "si" + plus-que-parfait to undo it, then land on the imagined result in the conditionnel passé — sometimes finishing with a conditionnel présent to show a lasting present effect.

examples.french: J'ai raté mon train ce matin-là. Si je ne l'avais pas raté, je ne t'aurais jamais rencontrée.
examples.english: I missed my train that morning. If I hadn't missed it, I would never have met you.

examples.french: Nous avons déménagé cette année-là. Si nous n'avions pas déménagé, nous vivrions ailleurs aujourd'hui.
examples.english: We moved that year. If we hadn't moved, we would live somewhere else today.

examples.french: Il a dit non par peur. S'il avait dit oui, tout aurait été différent.
examples.english: He said no out of fear. If he had said yes, everything would have been different.

blocks.tip: You don't need every clause to be hypothetical — mixing a real fact with its imagined alternative is what makes the story land.

passages.title: Et si j'avais pris l'autre train ?
passages.french:
Il y a dix ans, j'ai raté mon train à la gare de Lyon.
Furieux, j'ai attendu deux heures sur le quai, sans savoir que ce retard allait tout changer.
Si j'avais pris le train prévu, je ne me serais jamais assis à côté de Nadia.
Nous avons parlé pendant tout le trajet, et depuis, nous ne nous sommes plus quittés.
Parfois, je me demande ce que serait devenue ma vie si j'étais arrivé à l'heure ce jour-là.
J'aurais probablement continué mon chemin sans jamais la connaître.
Dans cette autre vie, j'habiterais peut-être encore dans mon ancienne ville, seul, avec mes habitudes.
Qui sait si j'aurais été heureux, dans cet univers parallèle ?
Avec le recul, ce retard a été un vrai tournant, même s'il m'a rendu fou sur le moment.
Nadia dit souvent qu'à quoi bon regretter le passé, puisque tout s'est bien terminé.
Elle a raison : en fin de compte, le hasard fait parfois mieux les choses que nos plans.
Alors, sans regret, je pense encore à ce train raté, comme au début de mon histoire préférée.
passages.english:
Ten years ago, I missed my train at Gare de Lyon.
Furious, I waited two hours on the platform, not knowing that delay would change everything.
If I had caught the planned train, I would never have sat next to Nadia.
We talked for the whole journey, and we've never left each other since.
Sometimes I wonder what my life would have become if I had arrived on time that day.
I would probably have gone on my way without ever knowing her.
In that other life, I might still be living in my old city, alone, with my old habits.
Who knows if I would have been happy, in that parallel universe?
Looking back, that delay was a real turning point, even if it drove me crazy at the time.
Nadia often says what's the point of regretting the past, since everything turned out well.
She's right: ultimately, chance sometimes does things better than our plans.
So, without regret, I still think about that missed train, like the beginning of my favorite story.
